body.en:
• Matrix Dimensions for Multiplication: To multiply \( A_{m \times k} \times B_{k \times n} \), the inner dimensions MUST match (number of columns of \(A\) = number of rows of \(B\)). The product has dimensions \( m \times n \). Matrix multiplication is NOT commutative: \( AB \neq BA \) in general.
  • Matrix Determinant & Inverse: For a \( 2 \times 2 \) matrix \( \begin{pmatrix} a & b \\ c & d \end{pmatrix} \), \( \det(A) = ad - bc \). If \( \det(A) = 0 \), the matrix has NO inverse. To form \( A^{-1} = \frac{1}{ad-bc} \begin{pmatrix} d & -b \\ -c & a \end{pmatrix} \), swap the main diagonal and negate the off-diagonal entries!
  • Powers of \( i \) Cycle of 4: \( i^1 = i \), \( i^2 = -1 \), \( i^3 = -i \), \( i^4 = 1 \). To evaluate \( i^n \), divide \( n \) by 4 and look at the remainder: remainder 0 \( \implies 1 \), remainder 1 \( \implies i \), remainder 2 \( \implies -1 \), remainder 3 \( \implies -i \).
  • Vector Magnitude & Addition: Vector addition is component-wise: \( \langle u_1, u_2 \rangle + \langle v_1, v_2 \rangle = \langle u_1+v_1, u_2+v_2 \rangle \). Magnitude is \( |\vec{v}| = \sqrt{v_1^2 + v_2^2} \). Do not simply add magnitudes together!

A complex number \(z = a+bi\) has modulus \(|z| = \sqrt{a^2+b^2}\) and argument \(\theta = \arctan(b/a)\). Polar form: \(z = r(\cos\theta + i\sin\theta)\). Multiplying in polar: multiply moduli, add arguments.

question.en: Simplify \((2+3i)(1-i)\) and write in the form \(a+bi\).
If \(A = \begin{pmatrix} 2 & -1 \\ 3 & 4 \end{pmatrix}\) and \(B = \begin{pmatrix} 5 \\ -2 \end{pmatrix}\), what is the matrix product \(AB\)?

solution.en: The product of a \(2 \times 2\) matrix and a \(2 \times 1\) matrix is a \(2 \times 1\) matrix. Compute row by column: the first entry is \(2(5) + (-1)(-2) = 10 + 2 = 12\); the second entry is \(3(5) + 4(-2) = 15 - 8 = 7\). Thus \(AB = \begin{pmatrix} 12 \\ 7 \end{pmatrix}\).
